rows.what the ink shows: An open c is followed by a compact low a and compressed r joins; a detached rising acute stands above the final short e stroke. The acute and the low middle strokes support carré rather than comme.
The initial d has a distinct upright stem, followed by a separate raised apostrophe. The following low u and n are linked into the final horizontal exit stroke.
An opening curved parenthesis precedes two separate upright numeral strokes, and a curved closing parenthesis follows. The second numeral has no curved head or lower horizontal foot of a 2.

The short earlier word lies under a thick doubled black cancellation, separate from the later visible vraie to its right. A small upright survives near its right end, but the baseline letter sequence is concealed, so vrai cannot be independently recovered.

The cancelled word retains a tall descending f, a crossed t, an adjacent i dot, and a final dotted aire-like group. Several low joined strokes through the middle are crossed by the deletion, so the entire letter sequence and repeated n count remain uncertain even beside the uncancelled same-page occurrence.

Below the inserted and underlined opérateur, the old word retains a tall initial h, long low linked strokes, and a crossed middle stroke. Dense cancellation covers the terminal letters; the surviving ink is compatible with hermitien but does not independently resolve the whole word.

The word has a compact initial co group, low n join, crossed t, separate i dot, and a short compressed nue ending. There is no additional ment group or final crossed t; the crossed t and dotted i agree with the uncancelled continue lower on this page.

A compact overwritten patch lies below the preceding 0, with a detached dot above its right edge and several short downward remnants. The cancellation covers the letter body, and no distinct grave accent can be separated from it, so à remains uncertain.

The mapping symbol has two long rising uprights joined at the foot, both substantially taller than the following u beside Λ. Their capital-height extent favors U, although its cursive joins resemble a lowercase u.

Above h are a separate short upright 1, a slanting division stroke below and to its right, and an α with a small left body and two rightward arms. The additional upright and division stroke exclude a bare α.

The deleted lower line retains an initial curved hook, partial troughs and a curved right terminator beneath the separate upper insertion. Its heavy horizontal cancellation conceals the baseline letters, the subscripts, and the internal punctuation count; the entire proposed formula remains uncertain.
The small raised sign beside Λ has a compact left loop and a short right downstroke, matching the adjacent raised a beside the second Λ. There is no extended descending tail of q.
The raised group contains a short curved opening parenthesis, one straight upright 1 and a curved closing parenthesis. The neighboring F formula shows a visibly bent, wider 2, unlike this upright.
Under the horizontal strike are a compact initial e loop and a taller t shaft with its rightward return. The two-letter remnant is separate from the following c. à d.
